reasoning: Recent Texas Senate polling over the last 45 days shows a very tight race, with multiple late-July and early-August polls putting Democrat James Talarico slightly ahead of Republican Ken Paxton, while the polling average remains slightly Republican-leaning. Texas’s statewide Cook PVI is R+14, indicating a strongly Republican baseline even as the immediate Senate polls have narrowed.

sources.name: 254 Labs
sources.details: Texas Democrats' 254 Labs poll found Talarico leading Paxton 48% to 45% among 1,001 registered voters, a 3-point Democratic edge within the poll's margin of error.

sources.name: Texas A&M Bush School / ReconMR
sources.details: Texas A&M Bush School and ReconMR found Talarico leading Paxton 47% to 43%, a 4-point Democratic edge.

sources.name: Texas 2026 U.S. Senate Poll Tracker
sources.details: The Texas Politics Project poll tracker lists Bush School/Recon MR at Talarico +4, TSU/YouGov at Talarico +2, and Fox News at Talarico +3 in recent Texas Senate polling.

sources.name: Fox News / Beacon Research
sources.details: Fox News/Beacon Research found Talarico leading Paxton 51% to 48% among 1,006 registered voters, a 3-point Democratic edge.

sources.name: Texas Public Opinion Research
sources.details: Texas Public Opinion Research found Talarico ahead of Paxton 45% to 40%, a 5-point Democratic edge.

sources.name: Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research and Survey Center at Texas Southern University
sources.details: Texas Southern University’s Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research and Survey Center found Talarico leading Paxton 47% to 45%, a 2-point Democratic edge.

sources.name: Pollsmax Texas Senate polling average
sources.details: Pollsmax’s Texas Senate polling average shows 44.7% D to 46.2% R, giving Republicans a 1.5-point advantage.

sources.name: Pollsmax Texas Senate forecast
sources.details: Pollsmax’s Texas Senate forecast shows a 45.3% D to 46.2% R average, for a 0.9-point Republican edge.
